newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda Sept inflation rises to annualised 8.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Uganda Sept inflation rises to annualised 8.3 pct.

text.p: Uganda's annualised inflation rate rose in September due to price rises for food and a selection of other commodities, the central bank said on Monday.
Bank of Uganda (BOU) said in a report inflation rose slightly to 8.8 percent from 7.3 percent in August.
"Most of this increase was recorded in the prices of food items, particularly staple foods, fruits and vegetables, meat and poultry products," the central bank said.
Uganda's inflation rate has been falling due to the government's clampdown on its spending and good food yields helped by favourable weather through most of the year.
Officials in the agriculture ministry said on Monday the rise in food prices was temporary as they expected food crop harvests to increase in October.
The central bank report said the Ugandan shilling currency had weakened against the dollar in September, reaching 1,074.27 at the end of the month from 1,067.44 as at the end of August.
It blamed the slight decline in the shilling's worth on low hard currency inflows.

"This was mainly due to the shortage of tradable foreign exchange in the market. Throughout the month, the depreciation was smooth and Bank of Uganda did not intervene in the market," it said in the report.
The bank did not give projections on inflation or the expected trend of the Ugandan shilling for October.

The BOU report said Uganda's foreign reserves rose to a level where they could pay for imports to last up to 5.57 months by the end of August but did not have figures for September. When the reserves stood at $467 million at the end of April, they were enough to pay for 4.77 months of imports, records showed.

The BOU report said the total amount of currency in circulation fell to 199.9 billion shillings by the start of August, slightly down from 210.3 billion the month before. It had no figures for September.
The report said the central bank paid out $13.12 million in interest on the country's $3.2 billion debt in July, the latest figure availed in the report.
The central bank gave no forecasts for October.
